hypotheses.title: Cashflow Conversion Efficiency Derivative with Microstructure Reversal
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Ranks equities cross-sectionally by their ability to generate free cash flow and operational profitability per unit of capital. High cash-conversion equities possess structural pricing power and protection against macroeconomic tightening. Paired with 5-day mean-reversion liquidity buffer to capture short-term microstructure reversals.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if capital-intensive unprofitable companies outperform during speculative liquidity bubbles.

hypotheses.title: Idiosyncratic Low-Beta Anomaly with Liquidity Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Structural Betting-Against-Beta (BAB) phenomenon. Leverage-constrained institutional and retail market participants overpay for high-beta equities to attain lottery-like payoffs, systematically depressing their risk-adjusted returns relative to low-beta equities. Group-ranking low-beta names within subindustries captures this risk premium without taking unhedged sector tilts.
confounders: Unhedged market rallies where high-beta violently leads
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails during speculative market melt-ups where high beta heavily outperforms.

hypotheses.title: Options Flow Put-Call Volume Ratio Exhaustion Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Informed options order flow dynamics (Pan & Poteshman 2004). Abnormally high put-to-call trading volume signals institutional hedging against impending adverse downside events, depressing forward stock performance. Conversely, low put/call volume indicates constructive institutional call demand. Neutralizing within subindustry isolates directional options positioning from broad market sentiment.
confounders: Market maker delta hedging flow distortions
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if speculative put buyers are persistently wrong and suffer theta decay without price drops.
